text:
The unemployment rate of 9.5% and the policy rate near 0.17% point to mid-2009. Headline CPI at -1.19% YoY fits June–July 2009, since CPI bottomed around -2.1% in July 2009. Payrolls averaged -436k over three months, which fits June 2009 (April -700, May -350, June -460 roughly). The unemployment rate was 9.5% in June 2009.

The market data fit as well. The S&P 500 was up 7% in the month (June 2009 was about +0.2%, so that does not match), while 3m +13.1% (March to June) does match. In July 2009 the S&P rose about 7.6%, but unemployment was 9.4% then. Revised data, however, put the unemployment rate at 9.5% in July 2009 (the 9.5% was June's initial print, and the 9.4% for July was initial), so the figures are ambiguous. CPI YoY was -1.4% in June and -2.1% in July, so -1.19% does not fit either cleanly.

The 12m equity return of -20% fits July 2009, because July 2008 to July 2009 was about -20%. In June 2009 the 12m return was about -26%. The 1m +7% also fits July. Core CPI at 1.75% fits July 2009 as well. The 10-year yield at 3.67% fits July (3.5% at the end of July; 3.53% in June). The VIX at 25.4 fits July (end of July about 25.9). I therefore choose July 2009.
